subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: After the blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the optional ACP runtime contract additions for `modelExplicit` and `appliedModel` as the compatibility boundary for Codex ACP spawn defaults?
rationale: The repair crosses the ACP runtime contract and changes provider/model fallback behavior for existing setups; automation can fix the narrow bug, but accepting this contract shape is a maintainer compatibility call.

options.title: Accept additive contract after repair
options.body: Keep the optional fields, land the provenance-aware fix after the derived-thinking blocker and focused tests are addressed, and treat it as the intended ACP runtime compatibility boundary.

options.title: Keep the fix ACPX-local
options.body: Ask for a narrower implementation that avoids adding shared ACP runtime fields, accepting more local ACPX policy and less reusable provenance plumbing.

options.title: Pause for ACP contract redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers decide a broader ACP runtime model/thinking provenance contract across backends.

recommendation.title: Accept additive contract after repair
recommendation.body: Keep the optional fields, land the provenance-aware fix after the derived-thinking blocker and focused tests are addressed, and treat it as the intended ACP runtime compatibility boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR is assigned/requested to vincentkoc and current-main history routes the implicated ACPX/ACP spawn paths there.
